subject: Visibility retention and SIEM sanctioning for Globex VPC
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Richardson <trichardson@globex.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Visibility retention and SIEM sanctioning for Globex VPC

Hi Tom —

Following our call earlier, attaching a proposed evidence retention matrix and a short comment on SIEM handoff options for the Globex private VPC deployment. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm retention window targets by log class (auth, inference, audit, metric aggregates).
- Decide whether you want raw syslog/HEC ingest or pre-scrubbed/parity bundles.
- Clarify whether you require signed chain-of-custody bundles for audits (we can emit signed gzip bundles).

Quick notes on feasibility:
- Redistribution model: we provide a forwarder inside the VPC that can push to Splunk HEC (mutual TLS + per-customer token), S3 (VPC endpoint), or an SFTP server for signed evidence packets.
- Tracing: we support OTLP export to a customer-side collector over mTLS. We can also inject trace hooks that add the redwood.request-id to every span for trace correlation.
- Scrubbing: configurable scrub rules in the forwarder (PII regexes, token hashing). Scrubbed vs raw export is a policy decision for Globex.

Attachment: evidence-retention-matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — has proposed TTLs and example retention policy language for contracts.

If you can confirm the retention bands and whether your security team wants signed evidence packets, we’ll follow up with a short technical handshake and a runbook.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
From: Tom Richardson <trichardson@globex.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: SecOps Team <secops@globex.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Jun 2029 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Visibility retention and SIEM sanctioning for Globex VPC

Ava — thanks for the doc. A few quick questions from our security team:

1) Chain of custody: does the signed bundle include per-file checksums and a signed manifest? We’ll need that for our upcoming audit.
2) Retention bands: can you support separate retention for auth logs (required 24 months) vs inference traces (90 days)?
3) Redaction: can the forwarder apply token masking that preserves structure (e.g., replace tokens with stable hashes so we can dedupe)?

Also, do you have a SOC2 artifact or a short attestation we can drop into our procurement packet? If you can connect me with the person who owns evidence exports, we’ll schedule a technical handshake.

Tom Richardson
Senior Manager, IT Security — Globex Corporation
trichardson@globex.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Richardson <trichardson@globex.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Visibility retention and SIEM sanctioning for Globex VPC

Tom — hi, Kimberly here (platform engineering). Answering the technical bits so we can line up the handshake:

- Signed bundle: yes. Our evidence exporter emits a gzipped bundle that contains per-file SHA256 checksums and a signed manifest (PKCS7). We can optionally timestamp via an external TSA if you require.
- Retention by class: supported. The exporter labels files with class metadata (auth/inference/metrics). The retention controller can apply TTLs per-class (24 months for auth, 90 days for traces) and will handle lifecycle transitions to cold storage (S3 Glacier) if needed.
- Redaction/hashing: forwarder supports stable hashing with a customer-provided salt (so you can dedupe while not exposing raw tokens). We also support regex-based scrub rules and field-level redaction for JSON logs.

Exporting options (choose one):
- Splunk HEC over private peering: immediate ingest, per-token ACLs, recommended for near-real-time SIEM.
- S3 push (VPC endpoint): periodic bundles (hourly/daily) with signed manifests. Good for custody/exchange model.
- SFTP/Aspera drop: secure batch export for audit teams.

Attachment: siem-handshake-checklist.pdf — checklist we use during customer handshakes (networking ports, token rotation cadence, expected latency for HEC).

Next steps: if Globex wants signed evidence for audits, we’ll need to confirm key exchange method (customer-managed KMS or Redwood-supplied) and network routing for the chosen export option.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

2) By 2029-07-09 — Redwood to provide detailed network runbook (ports, CIDR whitelists) and key-exchange options. Owner: Kimberly.
3) By 2029-07-12 — Technical handshake call (30m) to validate HEC token exchange and example manifest. Invitation to follow.
4) By 2029-07-19 — If signed-bundle route chosen, legal/DPA addendum to be reviewed. I’ll loop in legal.
